**9 issues found** across 220 files

**Note:** This PR contains a large number of files. Free-tier reviews are limited to 40 files per PR, so some files may not have been reviewed. cubic prioritises the most important files to review. Paid plans can review more files.

<details>
<summary>Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues)</summary>

```text

Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately.


<file name="langfn/python/langfn/agents/plan_execute.py">

<violation number="1" location="langfn/python/langfn/agents/plan_execute.py:47">
P2: `max_execution_steps=0` is ignored because `or` falls back to `len(plan)`. Use an explicit `None` check so zero is enforced correctly.</violation>
</file>

<file name="langfn/python/langfn/evaluation/dataset.py">

<violation number="1" location="langfn/python/langfn/evaluation/dataset.py:22">
P2: Malformed dataset items can leak raw `pydantic.ValidationError` instead of LangFn `ValidationError`, causing inconsistent error handling for callers.</violation>
</file>

<file name="langfn/python/langfn/mcp/stdio.py">

<violation number="1" location="langfn/python/langfn/mcp/stdio.py:55">
P2: `timeout_s or self.close_timeout_s` ignores explicit `0` timeouts; use an explicit `None` check so caller-provided values are honored.</violation>

<violation number="2" location="langfn/python/langfn/mcp/stdio.py:57">
P1: On shutdown timeout, the subprocess is left running and `_proc` is already cleared, which can leak orphan MCP child processes.</violation>
</file>

<file name="langfn/.conduct/release-gate.md">

<violation number="1" location="langfn/.conduct/release-gate.md:28">
P3: Remove “release artifacts” from this criterion; the gate only checks docs for absolute paths.</violation>
</file>

<file name="langfn/python/langfn/core/types.py">

<violation number="1" location="langfn/python/langfn/core/types.py:14">
P2: `total_tokens` should be derived from prompt/completion counts, not stored independently; the new field can drift and return incorrect usage totals.</violation>
</file>

<file name="langfn/python/langfn/mcp/client.py">

<violation number="1" location="langfn/python/langfn/mcp/client.py:23">
P2: Wrap `httpx` request failures and rethrow as `MCPTransportError` so transport errors have a consistent error type.</violation>
</file>

<file name="langfn/python/langfn/http/auth.py">

<violation number="1" location="langfn/python/langfn/http/auth.py:29">
P2: The bare `except Exception` silently swallows all errors from `_authenticate` (including programming bugs in the user-supplied `validate_bearer_token` callback) and converts them to a 401. Consider narrowing the catch or logging the exception so configuration/coding errors don't silently masquerade as auth failures.</violation>

<violation number="2" location="langfn/python/langfn/http/auth.py:39">
P1: `validate_auth_session(session)` can raise `AuthValidationError` (a subclass of `Exception`) when the dict is malformed, but this call sits outside the `try/except` block. An invalid dict from a custom `validate_bearer_token` callback will surface as an unhandled 500 instead of a 401.</violation>
</file>
```

</details>
